description:
Establish compatible shift and coding-permutation baselines. Establish reproducible operation-equivalent external baselines without changing production kernels.

## Background

Arbitrary zero-fill shifts, circulant rotations, puncturing and interleaving need separate semantic mappings. AFF3CT and other surveyed coding sources may expose some mappings but are not automatic substitutes for bit-vector operations.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Satisfy the [Zen 3 measurement contract](dev/active/1a379447-zen3-cpu-performance/measurement-contract.md) for correctness, reproducible release benchmarks, comparison validity and adoption; receipts pin its committed version, the frozen protocol and the cell addendum. Include mandatory before/after evidence for production changes and preserve negative outcomes.

- [hard] REQ-02: Survey and pin applicable open-source coding permutation paths, starting with AFF3CT, and identify the exact operation/layout, standards mapping, build and selected backend. Preserve explicit unmatched results for arbitrary shifts where no equivalent external API exists.

- [hard] REQ-03: Validate zero-fill versus wrap behavior, offset ranges, canonical bit order, tails and standards-defined output permutations in any adapter. Include packing and cross-lane conversion costs in comparable cells.

- [hard] REQ-04: Commit frozen family addenda and internal/external baseline receipts for measured-relevant operation cells, including scalar/compiler controls. Record all inapplicable mappings without forcing unrelated arithmetic into the scorecard.

## Notes

Pin exact source and build identities in the family addendum. Preserve unavailable, incompatible and losing arms rather than substituting a different operation.

Source references: [Cassagne2019].
title: Establish compatible shift and coding-permutation baselines
